questions.question: A heading must render no smaller than 14px, ideally 2.5vw, and never above 22px — in one declaration: `font-size: ___(14px, 2.5vw, 22px)`. Which function fills the blank?
questions.explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) returns the preferred value bounded below by min and above by max.

questions.question: To ship 2x product images only on Retina-class screens, a dev writes `@media (min-___: 2dppx)`. Which media feature fills the blank?
questions.explanation: The resolution media feature tests output-device pixel density in dppx or dpi, enabling density-conditional assets.

questions.question: A product card restyles at 400px based on its sidebar slot's width rather than the viewport, via `@container (min-width: 400px)`. Which CSS feature is this?
questions.explanation: Container queries let an element react to the size of its containment context instead of the viewport.

questions.question: Product thumbnails must keep a 4:3 box while their width flexes, replacing the old padding-top hack, via `___: 4 / 3`. Which property fills the blank?
questions.explanation: aspect-ratio fixes a box's width-to-height proportion so one dimension follows the other responsively.

questions.question: Instead of writing `1fr 1fr 1fr`, a dev condenses the track list to `___(3, 1fr)` in grid-template-columns. Which function fills the blank?
questions.explanation: repeat(count, tracks) generates repeated track patterns, pairing naturally with auto-fit and auto-fill for responsive grids.

questions.question: On a 1080 x 1920 portrait phone, a hero is sized at `50vmin`. How many pixels is that?
questions.explanation: vmin resolves against the smaller viewport dimension (1080px), so 50vmin = 50% x 1080 = 540px.

questions.question: On the same 1080 x 1920 phone, a banner is sized at `20vmax`. How many pixels is that?
questions.explanation: vmax resolves against the larger viewport dimension (1920px), so 20vmax = 20% x 1920 = 384px.

questions.question: An lists `hero-480.jpg 480w, hero-1200.jpg 1200w` so the browser downloads only the size it needs. Which attribute supplies these candidates?
questions.explanation: srcset declares candidate images with width or density descriptors; the browser picks the best fit for its viewport and pixel density.

questions.question: A hero must serve WebP with a JPEG fallback plus a cropped, art-directed mobile version via nested <source> tags. Which element wraps them?
questions.explanation: evaluates its children in order — by media or type — before falling back to the .

questions.question: A stylesheet must apply rules only to wide screens held sideways: `@media (min-width: 768px) ___ (orientation: landscape)`. Which keyword joins the conditions?
questions.explanation: The `and` keyword chains media conditions so all must match; a comma means OR and `not` negates.

questions.question: A component's @container rules silently do nothing until its wrapper opts in via `___: inline-size`. Which property creates the query context?
questions.explanation: container-type (inline-size, size, or normal) marks an element as a query container that descendants can measure against.

questions.question: With several nested containers on the page, a rule must hit only the 'sidebar' one via `@container sidebar (min-width: 300px)`. Which property assigned that container's name?
questions.explanation: container-name labels a query container so @container <name> rules resolve against that specific ancestor.

questions.question: A card inside a 500px-wide container sets `font-size: 4cqi`. What is the computed font size?
questions.explanation: 1cqi equals 1% of the container's inline size; 4% x 500px = 20px.

questions.question: A carousel must skip its slide animations for users whose OS asks for less motion, gated by `@media (___: reduce)`. Which media feature fills the blank?
questions.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion matches when the user requests minimal animation, letting sites honor vestibular and accessibility needs.

questions.question: A full-screen hero sized in `vh` jumps when the mobile URL bar hides; the dev switches to a unit following the currently visible height. Which unit?
questions.explanation: dvh is 1% of the dynamic viewport height, resizing as mobile browser chrome expands or collapses; svh and lvh pin the extremes.

questions.question: A site's nav collapses into a three-line icon whose menu slides in from the edge on phones. Name this navigation pattern.
questions.explanation: The hamburger menu hides navigation behind a three-bar icon, revealing it as an overlay or slide-in panel.

questions.question: A developer writes base styles for phones, then adds `@media (min-width: 768px)` layers for larger screens. Which responsive philosophy is this?
questions.explanation: Mobile-first starts with small-screen styles and progressively enhances via min-width media queries.

questions.question: At exactly 1024px a layout jumps from two columns to three via a media query. What is the 1024px point called?
questions.explanation: A breakpoint is the viewport width at which a media query changes the layout.

questions.question: A designer prefers `svh` over `vh` so a hero section never hides behind mobile browser toolbars. What does svh size to?
questions.explanation: svh equals 1% of the small viewport height, which assumes browser UI is fully expanded.

questions.question: A UX team serves dark-theme styles automatically when the OS is in dark mode. Which media feature detects that preference?
questions.explanation: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) matches when the user requests a dark color scheme.
